issues.title: What a random primary key costs in Postgres
issues.html:
#​673 — November 11, 2026


Web Version



🕒 Fingers crossed, the final release of Postgres 19 lands next week (Thursday, November 19), so we may hold the next issue back a day or two to cover it properly. If next week's newsletter arrives a little later than usual, that's why. :-)
__
Your editor, Peter Cooper



Postgres Weekly





UUIDv4 vs UUIDv7: What a Random Primary Key Costs — The difference is minimal if the index fits in memory, but grows rapidly as it outgrows the cache! In a memory-constrained benchmark, UUIDv4 inserts ran at two-thirds the rate of an ordered key and generated more WAL. Nikolay explains why and shares some catches in switching to uuidv7().

Nikolay Samokhvalov (PostgresAI)



Your Retention Job Shouldn’t Be a Four-Hour DELETE — Purging old rows with DELETE bloats the table, hammers WAL, and leaves VACUUM behind. TimescaleDB partitions by time, so retention drops whole chunks in milliseconds. Same Postgres, same SQL. Start on Tiger Cloud with a $1000 credit.

Tiger Data (creators of TimescaleDB) sponsor



Is Postgres Really Winning? — Postgres is the only top four database gaining ground in the DB-Engines rankings and might pass SQL Server soon, but it measures 'popularity', not production use. In part two, Dave looks further afield, at developer surveys, acquisitions, and what AI tools reach for by default. In short, things continue to look bright for Postgres.

Dave Stokes



IN BRIEF:

  • ⏰ Postgres's quarterly minor releases are due tomorrow, alongside Postgres 19 RC2. The draft announcement lists 140+ fixes and some post-update reindexing steps. Note that 14.25 will be Postgres 14's final release.

  • Xata is joining ClickHouse, whose Managed Postgres service went GA the same day. Meanwhile, EDB has acquired Altinity, a major ClickHouse contributor.

  • Google has unveiled AlloyDB Express, a scale-to-zero tier of its Postgres-compatible database that spins up in seconds and is aimed at prototyping and coding agents. It's in preview, with a free tier.

  • 🗓️ Tomorrow (November 12, 5pm GMT), there's a free Postgres Meetup for All online meetup where Adyen's Huseyin Demir will share what went right and wrong upgrading a huge Postgres fleet to v18 with logical replication.

  • 🇧🇪 The Postgres devroom at FOSDEM 2027 takes place on January 30 in Brussels. The CFP is open until November 28.



Why VACUUM Doesn't Shrink Your Postgres Indexes — A page-by-page look, using pageinspect, at why VACUUM thins out B-tree index pages but can't shrink the index, and why sequential keys don't refill the gaps. There's also an interactive visualizer to try it on a tiny tree yourself.

Radim Marek



An Index Scan Is Only Half the Story: How On-Disk Ordering Affects Performance — A look at why an identical index scan can become far slower after a migration involving a parallel data load. Richard shares a ctid query to help detect the problem.

Richard Yen



What Postgres is Waiting For (and Why Dashboards Can't Tell You) — Wait event dashboards work by sampling, so they can be right about where time goes overall, yet wrong about why one request is slow.

Dmitry Fomin (PostgresAI)



📄 A Database Per Git Worktree That Barely Uses Any Disk Space – Using Postgres 18's file_copy_method = clone on a copy-on-write filesystem like APFS or Btrfs. Dennis Paagman

📄 Our 'Default' postgresql.conf, Step by Step – The baseline Data Egret usually starts with when setting up or taking over a cluster, beginning with connection settings. Ilya Kosmodemiansky (Data Egret)

📊 Thirteen Small Measurements on Postgres 18 – Such as an unindexed foreign key turning a 13ms cascading delete into a 3.6 second one. Hollis Varden

📊 json vs jsonb: Size and Speed, Measured Chris van Eijk



RELEASES AND CODE:





  • PG Observability Map – An interactive map of Postgres's architecture (see above) where you can hover over a component to see which stats views and functions cover it. Inspired by Alexey Lesovsky's pgstats.dev diagram (which seems to be down).

  • Supavisor 2.10 – Supabase's multi-tenant Postgres connection pooler adds a setting to log or reject session-level SET, LISTEN, advisory locks and temp tables in transaction mode.

  • PgQueuer 2.0 – A Postgres-backed job queue for Python, built on LISTEN/NOTIFY and FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. (Docs.)

  • 🔒 pgx 5.12 – The popular Postgres driver for Go fixes SQL injection in certain simple-protocol batches and a server-authentication bypass affecting some connection settings.

  • pgstream 1.6 – Xata's replication and CDC tool fixes a bug where a restart could skip committed transactions.



📰 Classifieds



🔍 A read-only agent for slow Postgres queries. Faster queries without manual triage, bigger instances, or extra replicas. Free & open source.

WarpBuild infrastructure runs GitHub Actions twice as fast at half the cost. Get $50 in free credits with code START50.

⚡ Rebase is an open-source backend for Postgres: REST, auth, realtime and storage, with your access rules enforced by Postgres RLS.



AND FINALLY: WHO'S INSIDE THE ELEPHANT?





Don't Dream It, Be It! — Slonik, Postgres's mascot, turns up at many Postgres events, but who's in the suit? At last month's PGConf.EU it was Laurenz Albe, who reports that it's hot, you can't see your feet, but everybody wants a photo. His advice to first-time attendees who don't know anyone is… volunteer!

Laurenz Albe (CYBERTEC)

issues.title: Postgres 19's built-in bloat cleanup
issues.html:
#​672 — November 4, 2026


Web Version



Postgres Weekly





Postgres 19's REPACK: Built-In, Online Bloat Cleanup — Craig's favorite new Postgres feature is the one he thinks DBAs will care about most. REPACK folds VACUUM FULL and CLUSTER into one command and adds a CONCURRENTLY mode that keeps the table readable and writable, using logical decoding (a la pg_squeeze). He digs into its benefits and how to use it here.

Craig Kerstiens (Snowflake)



⭐ Postgres 19 remains on track for November 19, with RC2 due on November 12. Jonathan Katz has posted the draft press release for review, and the draft release notes continue to expand.



Sub-Second Personalization on One Lakehouse — Live demo: See how EDB Postgres AI delivers sub-second next-best-action on one copy of data in Apache Iceberg. Postgres, WarehousePG and ClickHouse share one catalog, with no pipelines between engines. Watch the demo.

EDB sponsor



Getting Rid of a 4 Terabyte Table Efficiently — How do you get rid of a 4 TB table on a primary with ten replicas with as little impact as possible? Radim compares the obvious DROP TABLE approach against batch deletes and a copy-and-swap, with the measured pros and cons of each.

Radim Marek



💡 In a similar vein, NexHealth has written up how they moved 4 TB out of a live Postgres database into its own Aurora cluster with no downtime.



IN BRIEF:

  • Want to ease into contributing to Postgres? Paul Jungwirth is running a patch review workshop where small teams will get to review a patch, with committers like Robert Haas critiquing the reviews. You can sign up here.

  • 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 Jimmy Angelakos recaps October's Postgres Edinburgh meetup, where Elizabeth Christensen covered what's new in Postgres 18 and 19.

  • Supabase has opened a public beta of OrioleDB and a private alpha of Multigres. OrioleDB's alternative Postgres storage engine needs no VACUUM, but it's not production-ready yet.

  • CloudNativePG is now a CNCF 'incubating' project. Gabriele Bartolini tells the project's story from its 2019 start at 2ndQuadrant to ~247 million operator downloads today.



Burnt TOAST: Why DBAs Dread Large Text Columns — A tour of how Postgres stores oversized column values, with benchmarks showing why keeping the heap small can speed up scans and updates that leave those values untouched, and why fetching them can still be expensive.

Shaun Thomas (pgEdge)



💡 Sticking to the TOAST theme, Franck Pachot ponders: do TOAST's compression and out-of-line thresholds suit typical JSONB document sizes?



'server closed the connection unexpectedly' Explained and Measured — Chris reproduces connection failures across six clients on Postgres 13, 15, 17 and 18, showing why the same failure produces different diagnostics, and why a lost connection during a COMMIT can leave the outcome uncertain.

Chris van Eijk



📄 Logical Replication Beyond One Writer – A walkthrough of building multi-region replication, testing failover and handling schema changes, with a runnable Docker lab. Dimitri Fontaine

📊 Benchmarking Vector Search in Six Database Engines – Postgres and pgvector go up against MongoDB, MariaDB, AliSQL and Valkey. Evgeniy Patlan (Percona)

📄 How Replication Slots Can Fill Your Disk Anugya Sinha (Microsoft)

📄 How Real is 'Autonomous Postgres'? Vibhor Kumar (EDB)



📰 Classifieds



📺 New 4-hour freeCodeCamp course: Watch a 1.6-second Postgres query drop to 10 ms with TimescaleDB continuous aggregates.



RELEASES AND CODE:





  • pgModeler 2.0 (above) – Billed as "the biggest release in the history of the project", the database modelling tool gets a multi-scene canvas and Postgres 18 support, but moves import, diff and SQL execution to a paid 'Plus' edition.

  • Melange – Compiles Zanzibar-style, relationship-based authorization from OpenFGA models into PL/pgSQL functions, so a permission check is just a SELECT check_permission(...) away, with no separate service or store.

  • 🌐 PostGIS 3.7.0 – The geospatial extension (now targeting Postgres 19) adds coverage edges, Float16 rasters and faster ST_DWithin. Postgres 12/13 support is dropped, and the geocoder and address standardizer move to separate repos.

  • 🔒 PostgreSQL Anonymizer 3.3 – Dalibo's data-masking extension fixes 12 vulnerabilities and existing users are urged to upgrade.

  • 🔒 pgAdmin 4 v9.19 – Fixes 15 CVEs. Server-mode users should upgrade, setting two new admin allowlists first.

  • Postgres.js 4.0 – Node.js driver rewritten with a scheduler to stop slow queries blocking fast ones, SCRAM channel binding and two security fixes.

  • TimescaleDB 2.31 – Tiger Data's time-series extension gains a new integer compressor (off by default for now, but expected to be on by default in 2.32) that can make databases ~10% smaller and typical queries ~50% faster.

  • pg_duckdb 1.2.0 – The DuckDB-in-Postgres extension moves to DuckDB 2.0 and adds initial Postgres 19 support. It's 'not ready for production use' for now.

  • pg_lion 0.3 – A bitmap-based inverted index type (inspired by roaring bitmaps, hence the name!) for faster counts, facets and GROUP BY on large tables.

  • Reylo 0.7 – Import plain .sql files into TypeScript with types inferred from your database. From the creator of Zod.

issues.title: Why a DBA said no to one column
issues.html:
#​671 — October 28, 2026


Web Version



Postgres Weekly





'Region': A Lesson in Data Integrity — One of Lætitia's coworkers added a free-text region column and planned to validate it in app code, but Lætitia wouldn't approve it. Here she makes a case for keeping rules in the database with a look at domains, enums, CHECK constraints and lookup tables, and how to add constraints on large tables without blocking traffic.

Lætitia Avrot



CREATE INDEX on 100M Vectors in Under Two Hours — HNSW indexes on large pgvector tables use lots of memory and can take days to build. Meet pg_vectorsearch: an open-source alternative for existing vector columns. At 100M vectors: a 25 GB index and 6 ms queries at 95% recall. See the benchmarks.

Tiger Data (creators of TimescaleDB) sponsor



📖 PostgreSQL 18 Query Optimization: A Free 199-Page Book — Postgres Pro's query tuning course, reshaped into a compact book that's now in English. It covers how the planner works, access methods, join strategies, statistics, reading execution plans and tuning approaches. Here's the PDF.

Pavel Tolmachev (PostgresPro)



IN BRIEF:

  • Microsoft has started pitching SQL Server to Postgres developers as an 'upgrade', touting its 32,767-connection limit. SQL Server expert Brent Ozar isn't buying it, and Microsoft's author pops up in the comments to argue back.

  • 🇺🇸 PgDay Boston 2027 takes place on April 10, 2027 at Tufts University. Registration is open, as is the CFP (until January 15).

  • 🇺🇸 Postgres Day SF is a free meetup (registration needs approval) at PlanetScale's San Francisco office on November 4, celebrating 30 years of Postgres with Bruce Momjian and Fabrizio Mello.

  • 📅 POSETTE 2027, Microsoft's annual virtual Postgres event, returns on March 30-31, 2027. No CFP yet.



Why I Don't Trust ON DELETE CASCADE — One big cascading DELETE plus a routine migration can freeze writes to a table. Tom explains the lock queue behind it, some replication traps, and why he prefers soft deletes.

Tom Pang (PlanetScale)



How a Read Replica Almost Took Down Its Primary Database — Google Cloud grows disks automatically so Photoroom wasn't worried about space. Then a backfill left a BI replica so far behind that the primary held 31.7TB of WAL for it. The disk grew close to a hard limit, and shrinking it meant downtime.

Marek Zaremba-Pike (Photoroom)



Moving 74GB Off RDS with a Week-Long Rollback Window — Prisma moved its console's database off RDS with logical replication and no write pause, then ran replication in reverse so it could fall back to RDS for a week.

Siket and Datta (Prisma)



📄 Your App Doesn't Need Postgres Superuser – Superuser can run commands on the server, so here's what to grant apps and agents instead. Umair Shahid (Stormatics)

📄 Postgres 19 is Late, and It's AI's Fault Robert Haas

📄 Tuning Postgres for Analytics – Slides and transcript from PGConf.EU on running reports against your app's database without slowing it. Karen Jex



🎙️ Karen also joined Claire Giordano on the Talking Postgres podcast to talk about her path from Oracle DBA to Postgres contributor.



📰 Classifieds



⚡ Rebase turns your Postgres into an API and an admin panel your team can use. Our own CRM: 23 tables, zero hand-written admin screens.

⏱️ One 5-row lookup table turned a 0.3 ms Postgres query into 467 ms. Find yours before prod does. Now in preview.



RELEASES AND CODE:





pgVolvra: Flashback-Style 'Undo' for Bad UPDATEs and DELETEs — Trigger-based row history that lets you preview and reverse a bad statement or migration by transaction ID. Plain SQL with no superuser needed, so it works on managed Postgres too. GitHub repo.

Muhammad Aqeel (pgEdge)



pgrust 0.4 Beta: The Rust Rewrite of Postgres Opens Up — The experimental Rust reimplementation of Postgres adds a new JIT engine, transactional columnar tables and automatic memory sizing (no more work_mem tuning?).

Michael Malis



💡 ClickHouse pulled pgrust from ClickBench in September over per-query code and caching. With v0.4's source public, it's back in, and central to a benchmark-overfitting debate.



pg_pinecone: Pinecone's Vector Index for pgvector Columns — A new extension that indexes existing pgvector columns using IVF and RaBitQ quantization, applying filters during the search. Its native engine runs locally on Postgres 17 and 18, and Pinecone reports a 136MB index vs 2GB for HNSW on 1M vectors. GitHub repo.

Daddala and Mahanna (Pinecone)





  • pg_hdr_histogram 1.0 (above) – Store value distributions (e.g. latencies) as compact HDR histograms, then query p99-style percentiles and merge them losslessly across time windows or servers, say.

  • mcdview – Turn a Postgres schema dump (or a Prisma, pgModeler or Rails schema) into a searchable, shareable interactive ER diagram. You can try it online or see an example of its output here.

  • Citus 14.3 – The distributed Postgres extension adds sorted-merge execution for multi-shard ORDER BY queries and per-shard pruning of OR clauses.

  • SPQR 3.2 – Yandex's Postgres sharding router adds spqrmigrate, a schema migration tool.
